components.description: Softmax Jacobian sensitivity to Jacobian-guided noise injection and its results

nodes.name: Attention is sensitive to quantization
nodes.description: The self-attention mechanism is particularly sensitive to quantization errors, and error propagation is highly pronounced in attention layers of quantized models.

nodes.name: Softmax Jacobian is dense and state-dependent
nodes.description: Unlike a linear layer whose Jacobian is a fixed weight matrix, the softmax Jacobian J_S(z) is dense and strictly state-dependent, so error amplification varies with the input.

nodes.name: Spread attention is sensitive, concentrated is saturated
nodes.description: When attention concentrates on a single token the Jacobian norm approaches zero (saturated, safe), while attention spread over two or more tokens lies in sensitive regions where quantization errors are amplified.

nodes.name: Bounding quantization error needs Jacobian norm
nodes.description: The quantization-induced error in attention probabilities can be bounded by constraining the spectral norm of the softmax Jacobian.

nodes.name: Spectral norm bounded by logit Hessian trace
nodes.description: Near a local optimum, ||J_S||_2 <= sqrt(Tr(logit Hessian)/lambda_min), so regularizing the trace of the logit Hessian bounds the Jacobian and quantization error.

nodes.name: Gaussian logit noise implicitly regularizes Hessian
nodes.description: Minimizing expected loss under zero-mean isotropic Gaussian logit perturbation N(0, sigma^2 I) matches Hessian-trace regularization with strength lambda = sigma^2/2.

nodes.name: Jacobian Frobenius norm has closed form
nodes.description: For p = softmax(z), ||J_S||_F^2 = ||p||_2^2 - 2||p||_3^3 + ||p||_2^4, computable with element-wise operations and negligible forward overhead.

nodes.name: Noise variance derived from Jacobian norm
nodes.description: Jacobian-guided noise injection sets row-wise noise std sigma_i = alpha * sqrt(E[||J_S||_F^2]), concentrating regularization on sensitive positions, updated every T steps, clamped, and disabled at inference.

nodes.name: Method gives PTQ gains across families
nodes.description: Jacobian-guided noise injection improves quantized performance consistently for Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B under AWQ, GPTQ and SpinQuant, without significantly degrading full-precision accuracy.

nodes.name: Large gains on SigLIP at W4A4
nodes.description: On SigLIP at W4A4, noise injection recovers up to +9% accuracy with ERQ and up to +37% with RepQViT, with gains growing as bit-width decreases.

nodes.name: Method also helps QAT
nodes.description: Noise injection improves over the QAT baseline for SigLIP, so it is usable with existing QAT pipelines.

nodes.name: Moderate alpha is best
nodes.description: In SigLIP W4A4 QAT, alpha in [0.5, 1.0] works best (alpha = 0.5 gives 31.37% vs 30.31% baseline) and performance drops to 27.69% at alpha = 50.

isolated_nodes.name: No inference overhead
isolated_nodes.description: The method adds no inference-time overhead and matches baseline performance at fp16.

isolated_nodes.name: Perplexity gain up to 40%
isolated_nodes.description: The method gives up to +37% relative accuracy gains and improves relative WikiText perplexity by up to 40% in low-bit settings.

isolated_nodes.name: Zero Jacobian norm is problematic
isolated_nodes.description: A zero Jacobian norm from single-token concentration degenerates to near-constant outputs and large logit magnitudes amplify quantization errors exponentially; noise injection discourages this collapse.

isolated_nodes.name: Low bits and outliers worsen degradation
isolated_nodes.description: Quantization degradation is more severe at 4-bit or below due to reduced capacity and activation outliers.

structural_reasoning: Theoretical chain from softmax sensitivity through Hessian regularization to the noise design, followed by empirical results.
